claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Another claimant who lives with the child has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Another claimant who lives with the child has priority
circumstances: Another claimant who lives with the child has priority
Child is not in local authority care
Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to know about the children you're claiming for. 

**What is the age of the child (or children) you're claiming for?** 

Please tell me:
- How many children are you claiming for?
- What is/are their age(s)?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit eligibility depends significantly on the child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, they fall into the first category. Now I need to check a few more things to determine your eligibility. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Since Alex is 8 years old, I have one question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

For an 8-year-old, the answer is almost certainly "yes" since children this young wouldn't typically be in employment. Please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

For most primary school children, the answer would be "yes" - they wouldn't be receiving these benefits. Can you confirm this is the case for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is only 8 years old and still in primary school, I expect the answer is "yes" - they're not in any apprenticeship. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's only 8!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect. Let me move to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important eligibility requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet UK residency requirements?** There are several ways you might qualify:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - You live in the UK as your normal place of residence
2. **EU Settlement Scheme** - You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **Pre-settled status with certain conditions** - You have pre-settled status and meet certain criteria (such as working, seeking work, studying, or having sufficient resources)
4. **Crown servant abroad** - You work abroad as a Crown servant in certain qualifying circumstances

Which of these applies to you? Or do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK in Manchester. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. There are a few ways you can demonstrate this:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means:

1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex in the same household, OR
2. **Contributing to their upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care (this could include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.), OR
3. **Paying maintenance** - You make payments towards Alex's maintenance under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to you? I expect you live with Alex - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex at home. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example, could Alex's other parent or another family member be claiming? Or are you the sole claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex's other parent already claims Child Benefit for him, and Alex lives with them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Ah, I see - this is an important detail. Let me clarify the situation:

**So Alex lives with the other parent who is already claiming Child Benefit for him?** Does that mean Alex doesn't live with you, or does Alex live with both of you?

This matters because Child Benefit can typically only be claimed by one person for each child. If Alex lives primarily with the other parent and they're already claiming, that would affect your eligibility.

Can you clarify:
- Who does Alex live with primarily (or does he live with both parents equally)?
- Are you and the other parent in agreement about who should be claiming, or is there a dispute about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm sorry, I think I wasn't clear earlier. Alex does live with me here in Manchester. But his other parent, who also lives with us, is the one who's already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Ah, thank you for clarifying! So both you and Alex's other parent live together with Alex in Manchester, and the other parent is currently claiming Child Benefit for him.

This is an important situation. Let me ask:

**Are you and the other parent in agreement about the arrangement, or is there a dispute?** In other words:

- Do you both agree that the other parent should continue to be the sole claimant, OR
- Are you disputing who should be claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

This distinction is important because if there's a dispute between you and the other parent about who should claim, HMRC will need to make the final decision. But if you're both in agreement about the current arrangement, we can proceed differently.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're in agreement - they're the one claiming and that's fine. I was just curious about whether I could be eligible if I wanted to claim instead.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - you're asking a hypothetical question about your eligibility. That's useful information.

However, since you've confirmed that:
1. Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex
2. You're both in agreement with this arrangement
3. You're not actually looking to dispute or change the claim

This means that in the current situation, **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** because only one person can claim per child, and the other parent is already the designated claimant.

However, let me check what the decision tree says about this scenario to give you the complete picture.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Actually, I should clarify - the system is still following through the assessment. Since you mentioned you were curious about eligibility hypothetically, let me continue through the decision tree to give you a complete picture of what your eligibility would be if you were to claim instead.

**Is Alex currently living in any of these situations:**
- In hospital?
- In care (local authority care)?
- Being fostered?
- Living normally at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with us.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good, let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you and the other parent fully supporting Alex financially yourselves, without the council paying for his care or accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's care. We support him ourselves.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now I have all the information I need to give you a complete answer.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Based on my assessment of your situation, here's the outcome:

## **You Would Be ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

### Summary of Your Situation:
- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16 - qualifying age)
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (living with him)
- ✅ Alex is living normally at home with you
- ✅ The local council is not paying towards Alex's care

### Important Context:
Since the other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex and you're both in agreement with this arrangement, **only one of you can claim at a time**. Child Benefit can only be paid to one person per child. If you wanted to claim instead, the other parent would need to stop their claim, or you could discuss transferring the claim between you.

### If You Were to Claim:
Should you ever wish to apply or take over the claim, you would need to:
1. Apply online or by post using form CH2
2. Provide proof of your identity
3. Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
4. Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year
5. Payments would be made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you, that's really helpful! So just to confirm - I do meet all the eligibility requirements myself, it's just that only one of us can claim at a time, and since my partner is already claiming, I can't also claim right now. But if we wanted to switch it over to me, that would be possible because I am eligible, right?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Exactly! You've understood the situation perfectly. 

**Yes, that's correct:**
- ✅ You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ Only one person can claim per child at any given time
- ✅ Your partner is currently the claimant
- ✅ If you and your partner wanted to switch the claim to you in the future, that would be possible because you are eligible

You could contact HMRC or use the online system to transfer the claim between you if you ever wanted to make that change. It's a straightforward process when both parties agree.

Now let me formally record the eligibility outcome for this assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! The assessment is complete. You have confirmed eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. 

Thank you for working through this with me, and I'm glad I could help clarify your situation! If you have any other questions about Child Benefit in the future, feel free to ask.

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) Alex is 8 years old, which is under the qualifying age of 16; (2) Alex is not working full-time or in paid work; (3) Alex is not receiving benefits in their own right such as ESA or Universal Credit; (4) Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) The claimant normally lives in the UK (Manchester), meeting residency requirements; (6) The claimant is responsible for Alex by living with them in the same household; (7) Alex is living normally at home with the claimant; and (8) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.

All eligibility criteria are met: Alex is of qualifying age (under 16), not in disqualifying circumstances, the claimant meets residency requirements, is responsible for the child, and is not receiving council support. Currently, the other parent is claiming and both parents are in agreement with this arrangement. However, the claimant could request to transfer the claim to themselves if desired, as they meet all eligibility requirements. Only one claimant can receive Child Benefit per child at any time."]
